issues.t: Rusted steel brake lines can burst
issues.sym: The brake pedal suddenly sinks much lower than normal or goes nearly to the floor, sometimes with brake fluid dripping near a wheel or along the frame.
issues.why: The steel brake lines run along the frame where road salt and moisture collect. After many winters they rust from the outside until a line gives way under pressure.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. If the pedal feels low or soft, do not keep driving. Have a shop inspect every brake line along the frame and replace corroded sections, ideally with corrosion-resistant line.

issues.t: Dashboard gauges stick or read wrong
issues.sym: The speedometer, tachometer, fuel or temperature needles freeze, jump around, or sit at zero while driving.
issues.why: The tiny stepper motors that move each gauge needle wear out on this generation. GM addressed it with a service bulletin and extended coverage on some trucks.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether any coverage applies to your VIN. Otherwise a specialist can replace the stepper motors or rebuild the cluster.

issues.t: In-tank fuel pump wears out
issues.sym: A louder whine from the fuel tank, long cranking before it starts, sputtering under load, or the engine quitting while driving.
issues.why: The electric pump inside the tank wears out with age. Owners report it fails sooner on trucks often run with a low fuel level, since the fuel helps cool the pump.
issues.next: If the truck stalls or struggles to start, have fuel pressure tested before replacing parts. Keeping the tank above a quarter full may help the pump last.

issues.t: Knock sensor codes on the V8
issues.sym: Check-engine light with a knock sensor code, sometimes with slightly weaker performance or fuel economy.
issues.why: The knock sensors sit in the valley under the intake manifold. Water can collect there and ruin the sensors or their wiring, the rear one most often.
issues.next: Have the code confirmed. The fix usually means removing the intake to replace both sensors and the harness, and new intake gaskets at the same time.

issues.t: Blower motor resistor fails or burns its connector
issues.sym: The fan works only on high or on one speed, or stops entirely; sometimes a hot plastic smell from under the dash.
issues.why: The resistor that sets the fan speed overheats and fails, and on some trucks the heat damages its wiring plug. GM sold an upgraded harness for this.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Replace the resistor and check the connector for melting. If the plug is scorched, replace it too so the problem does not return.

issues.t: Front wheel speed sensor and hub failure
issues.sym: ABS and brake warning lights on together, the ABS kicking in at low speed, or a grinding hum from a front wheel.
issues.why: The front ABS speed sensors are built into the wheel hub assemblies, and they corrode or fail with the bearings. The usual fix is a new hub.
issues.next: Have the ABS codes read to find which wheel is at fault, and replace the hub assembly. Normal braking works but ABS will not until it is fixed.

issues.t: 4WD selector problems and Service 4WD light
issues.sym: A Service 4WD message, the 4WD buttons not responding, or the truck not shifting into or out of four-wheel drive.
issues.why: The dashboard 4WD switch and the transfer case encoder motor that shifts it are known weak points on these trucks.
issues.next: Have the codes read to tell a bad switch from a bad encoder motor. Avoid relying on 4WD in bad weather until it works properly.

issues.t: Clunk in the steering at low speed
issues.sym: A clunk or bump felt through the steering wheel during slow turns, like in parking lots, or looseness in the steering.
issues.why: The intermediate steering shaft has a sliding joint that dries out and wears. GM offered a re-grease kit, and worn shafts are replaced.
issues.next: Have the steering shaft checked so other causes like worn tie rods are ruled out. Lubricating or replacing the shaft usually stops the clunk.

issues.t: 4-speed automatic wears out
issues.sym: Slipping, flaring revs between gears, harsh or late shifts, losing certain gears, or the truck not moving in drive.
issues.why: The 4L60-E four-speed automatic in many of these trucks wears internally, especially with towing or heavy loads, and commonly needs a rebuild at higher mileage.
issues.next: Stop towing and get it checked at the first sign of slipping. Driving on a slipping transmission can turn a repair into a full rebuild.

issues.t: Heavy oil consumption
issues.sym: You need to add a quart or more between oil changes, the low-oil light comes on, and you may see blue smoke at startup or feel a misfire.
issues.why: Piston rings on this version of the 5.3L can clog, partly linked to the cylinder-shutoff fuel-saving system spraying oil. Oil gets past the rings and burns. GM issued bulletins and a class action followed.
issues.next: Check the dipstick at every fill-up and keep the oil full. Ask a dealer about GM's oil consumption bulletins; repairs may involve new pistons and rings.

issues.t: Lifter failure in cylinder-deactivation engines
issues.sym: A ticking or tapping from the top of the engine, a check-engine light with misfire codes, rough running, or power loss.
issues.why: The special lifters that let the engine shut off cylinders to save fuel can stick or collapse. A failed lifter can also damage the camshaft. There is no recall; a class action is pending.
issues.next: Get a misfire or new ticking checked quickly. Driving with a collapsed lifter can wipe out the camshaft and turn a smaller repair into a much bigger one.

issues.t: Loss of brake assist from vacuum pump
issues.sym: The brake pedal suddenly feels very hard and the truck takes longer to stop, sometimes with a brake warning message.
issues.why: The engine-driven vacuum pump that powers the brake booster can lose output over time. GM recalled the trucks for a software change that uses the ABS pump to help.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check for open recalls on your VIN and have the recall work done right away. If the pedal goes hard, press harder and get the truck inspected before regular use.

issues.t: One wheel may brake on its own
issues.sym: The truck pulls hard to one side or slows unexpectedly, often with ABS or stability warning lights.
issues.why: If a wheel speed sensor fails, the stability system can wrongly apply the brake at one wheel. GM recalled affected trucks for a software fix.
issues.next: If the truck pulls or brakes by itself, pull over safely. Check your VIN for the recall and have it repaired before regular driving.

issues.t: 8-speed automatic shudder and harsh shifts
issues.eng: 5.3L V8, 6.2L V8 and 2.7L turbo with 8-speed automatic
issues.sym: A vibration like driving over rumble strips at steady speeds with light throttle, plus clunky 1-2 shifts or a delay engaging Drive.
issues.why: The original fluid in the 8-speed automatic absorbed moisture and lost its friction qualities, making the torque converter clutch grab and slip. GM changed the fluid specification and updated software.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about GM bulletin 18-NA-355, which calls for a complete flush with updated fluid. It often cures the shudder if done before the converter is damaged.

issues.t: Driveshaft weld can separate
issues.sym: A new vibration or clunk from under the truck, then a sudden loss of drive power, possibly with damage underneath.
issues.why: A weld on the driveshaft joint may not have been made properly at the factory and can come apart. GM recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: If you feel a new driveline vibration, slow down and have it inspected. Check your VIN for the driveshaft recall.

issues.t: Rear wheels can lock up
issues.sym: The rear wheels suddenly lock or skid while driving, especially at lower speeds, sometimes with a transmission warning.
issues.why: A valve in the 10-speed automatic's control unit can stick, causing a sudden downshift that locks the rear wheels. GM recalled the trucks for a software update or valve body replacement.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and get it done before regular use. If the rear wheels skid, steer straight and come to a stop safely.

issues.t: 6.2L V8 internal engine failure
issues.sym: A knocking from inside the engine, a low oil pressure warning, rough running, loss of power, or the engine stopping entirely.
issues.why: Debris in oil passages and out-of-spec crankshafts and connecting rods on engines built from 2021 to mid-2024 can damage the bearings. GM recalled the trucks.
issues.next: Run your VIN through the recall lookup. If you hear knocking or see a low oil pressure warning, stop driving and have the truck towed to a dealer.

issues.t: Diesel coolant control valve failure
issues.sym: Check-engine light, and in some cases the temperature gauge climbing toward hot.
issues.why: The electronic valve that routes coolant around the diesel engine can fail. GM issued special warranty coverage to replace it.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether your VIN is covered. If the temperature climbs, stop and let the engine cool rather than pushing on.

issues.t: Missing transfer case part can lock the wheels (do-not-drive recall)
issues.sym: A sudden grab or lockup from the driveline, grinding from under the truck, or wheels that will not turn freely.
issues.why: A part can be missing inside the transfer case, which lets the drive components jam and lock the front or rear wheels.
issues.next: Do not drive the truck. Have it taken to a dealer for the recall repair, because wheels locking at speed can cause a crash.

issues.t: Rear axle cross pin can shift and lock the axle (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or knock from the rear axle, then a sudden bind or lockup of the rear wheels.
issues.why: The cross pin inside the rear differential may not have been heat treated properly, so it can move out of place and jam the gears.
issues.next: Stop driving and have the recall pin replacement done; a rear axle that locks up can send the truck sideways.

issues.t: Wheelchair restraint retractors may not lock (recall)
issues.sym: The restraint strap keeps paying out instead of locking, so a wheelchair is not held firmly in place.
issues.why: Retractors in certain aftermarket wheelchair restraint systems fitted to these trucks may not lock as designed.
issues.next: Only applies to trucks built with those mobility restraints; have them replaced under the recall before carrying anyone in a wheelchair.

issues.t: Cylinder deactivation lifter can collapse
issues.sym: A tick or tap from the top of the engine that does not go away when it warms up, a shaky idle, the check engine light on with a misfire on one cylinder, and sometimes a clear loss of power.
issues.why: The special lifters that shut cylinders off under light load can stick or collapse; a collapsed lifter stops opening its valve, can bend the pushrod and can wear the camshaft lobe flat.
issues.next: Get it diagnosed right away and keep driving to a minimum - once the camshaft lobe is damaged, a lifter job turns into a camshaft and sometimes a whole-engine job.
